shared_elements: carved relief on upright stone monolith
justification: A is a three-dimensional head with a reduced, schematic face (deep-set brow ridges, long nose, minimal mouth), whereas B is a flat relief-covered pillar bearing a horizontal register of crouching quadrupeds above a zigzag/meander band, then birds, a snake-like creature and a large bird facing left. The only real correspondence is the shared reliance on highly schematic, low-relief carving on upright stone with a vertical stacking of motifs; the actual subject matter, an isolated human head versus a multi-tiered animal frieze, does not overlap.
